pr_title: Fix partial reduce bug in ip_prefix
pr_body:
This stops us from applying the `min_doc_count` operation on partial
reduction. If run it on partial reduction then we filter out results
that might have more docs arrive.

Closes #89686
pr_comments: Hi @nik9000, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

OK, I see and I understand what is the issue. When we have partial reductions we don't want to filter results based on `min_doc_count` but wait until the final reduction. This way we know how many documents are there in total before filtering based on `min_doc_count`. Otherwise, filtering during partial reduction affects the total number calculated at the end, discarding results that should normally be ok. The following partial reductions might add more documents resulting in a value of doc count that is larger than `min_doc_count`.

LGTM.

comments: This looks to be a real bug with partial reduction of the ip prefix aggregation. I have a fix locally that passes the test. I'll add an explicit, non-randomized and more obvious test case and open an PR.

review_comments: These two lines are the actual fix.
This was backwards. I tend to use `assertThat` every time because if you write it backwards it'll fail to compile.
`IpPrefixAggregatorTests` is the first one of these not to support the deprecated high level rest client so I had to add support for that to this test.
This is the test that was failing. I made some minor modifications to it while I was tracking the issue.
I added this because it makes it *fairly* easy to make a precise test for the partial reduction, without involving the actual aggregator. See the last method on this class.
